clue.text: Throw drink over Labour leader after British PM's predecessor?

indicators.note: the drink-and-leader piece comes after the British-and-predecessor piece in the answer

parts.note: AM comes before PM on the clock, so it is what precedes PM

indicators.note: the drink is placed over, covering, the letter from Labour

parts.note: booze is slang for alcoholic drink

indicators.note: the leader of Labour is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A protester douses the Labour leader with a drink, in some story about a former prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM's predecessor' looks like a former prime minister, but it is the morning hours that come before PM. 'over' wraps the drink round L.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to confuse or disconcert them, which is exactly what tricking them does.

clue.text: See 25
Joke leader's assumed great power

indicators.note: assumed means taken on board, so the leader's name takes in the joke

parts.note: Theresa May was the UK's leader when this puzzle appeared; the 's stands for has
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A political leader's joke is said to have taken on enormous influence.
explanation.walkthrough: The leader is Theresa May, British prime minister when the puzzle appeared in 2019; 'assumed' puts the joke inside her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sovereign power and grandeur, as of a monarch, is what the word names.

clue.text: See 22 across
Spot, for the lady, some instruments

parts.note: a zit is a pimple or spot
something for the lady is hers, belonging to her

explanation.surface: Someone sets aside a few musical instruments with a woman in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: These are stringed instruments plucked while lying flat, so they are examples of instruments.

clue.text: Getting on, this setter is flipping barmy

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the setter's word is read upwards

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so this setter gives me
barking, as in barking mad, means barmy or crazy

explanation.surface: An ageing crossword setter admits to going completely mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping barmy' reads like a mild oath, but 'flipping' turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on a ship or a plane is boarding it, a synonym for setting off aboard.

clue.text: Change reversed, having shaved my dog

indicators.note: reversed means the remaining letters are read backwards
shaving takes off the edges, so the letters of my are trimmed from the outside

parts.note: to modify is to change
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notes a change in their dog after giving it a close shave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having shaved my' takes M and Y off the ends of MODIFY, leaving ODIF, which 'reversed' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the stock pet name for a dog, used of dogs in general.

clue.text: Join in search, interesting for a short while

indicators.note: in places the joining word inside the searching word

parts.note: to fish for something is to search for it
to add is to join on

explanation.surface: An invitation to help with a hunt that will only hold the attention briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something faddish is a passing craze, holding interest only briefly before fashion moves on.

clue.text: Style of drake, with cuss?

definitions.note: a 1950s greaser hairstyle swept back to a point is named after a male duck's rear, with a rude word for bottom

indicators.note: to style is to arrange or fashion, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: What hairdo would a male duck have, with a swear word attached?
explanation.walkthrough: A drake is a male duck, and the 1950s hairstyle's name contains a rude word for bottom, so the whole clue doubles as the definition; 'Style of' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The greased-back 1950s haircut meeting in a point at the nape is named after a duck's tail end.

clue.text: Don't allow supporter to see player

parts.note: to ban is to not allow
a joist is a beam supporting a floor or ceiling

explanation.surface: A fan is refused permission to watch a sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' looks like a sports fan, but it is a beam holding up a floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plays the banjo is a kind of instrumental player.

clue.text: Old bones alongside black garment

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
bones is old slang for dice, once carved from bone

explanation.surface: Ancient bones are laid out next to a dark item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bones' is old slang for dice.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's close-fitting upper garment, often laced, is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Creator, one upset about Hades

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the underworld's name
upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters of one are rearranged

parts.note: Dis is another name for Hades, the classical underworld

explanation.surface: A god of creation is distressed by the realm of the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the letters of 'one' into EON, and 'about' wraps that round the underworld's other name.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison invented the phonograph and much else, so he was a prolific creator.

clue.text: First: last of course is later, however

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the next word
however means in whatever way, so the letters of is later may be arranged any way

explanation.surface: A paradox: the end of the course comes first, however late it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'however' rearranges IS LATER into ARLIEST, after E from 'course'.
explanation.definitionFit: The soonest or initial instance of something is the first one.

clue.text: Throw a tantrum when baby eats plant

indicators.note: eats means takes inside, so the baby surrounds the planting word

parts.note: a pup is a baby animal such as a young dog or seal
to lay is to put or place something, as one plants it

explanation.surface: A toddler has a fit while munching on a houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: To misbehave or act up noisily is to make a scene, like a child having a fit.

clue.text: Vile profanities in opera lacking appeal

indicators.note: in places the swear words inside what is left of the opera
lacking means without, so the appeal letters are dropped from the opera

parts.note: Salome is an opera by Richard Strauss
SA is short for sex appeal
oaths are swear words

explanation.surface: An opera full of swearing and with no charm is judged repulsive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' is sex appeal, a crossword convention; 'lacking' removes it from the Strauss opera, leaving LOME, and 'in' puts the profanities inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vile is disgusting and hateful, the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Some way through introductory pieces, music finally stops

indicators.note: some way through means part of the way into, so a letter goes inside the pieces

parts.note: preludes are introductory pieces of music

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of music

explanation.surface: Partway through the opening numbers, the music comes to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives C from 'music', which goes inside PRELUDES.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to prevent or rule it out, stopping it happening.

clue.text: Sturdy case: more flexible parts sliding around

indicators.note: parts means separates, so the outer letters are pushed apart by the flexible word
the case of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: lither means more supple or flexible

explanation.surface: A sturdy box gives way to bendier components that move about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun for components, but it is a verb: the outer letters of 'Sturdy' are split by the flexible word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippery and moving like a snake, so prone to slithering about.

clue.text: Hitler's offensive struggle with weight?

definitions.meaning: the German counter-attack in the Ardennes in winter 1944 to 1945
a humorous phrase for dieting, fighting the spare tyre round the waist

explanation.surface: A dictator's attack is likened to someone trying to slim.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ardennes campaign got its name from the bulge in Allied lines, and dieters fight a bulge too.

clue.text: I appreciate that offer to cover characters central to plot in newspaper

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks

indicators.note: to cover means to enclose, so the offer goes round the central letters

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at auction

indicators.note: characters central to points to the middle letters of plot

explanation.surface: Someone thanks a paper for offering to cover the heart of a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British for thank you; the middle of 'plot' is LO, which BID covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular paper with a small page size and sensational stories is this kind of newspaper.

clue.text: Processing of ferric oxide, ultimately more intense

indicators.note: processing means working over, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the last letter of oxide

explanation.surface: A chemistry process: refining iron oxide until it ends up stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E from 'oxide', which joins FERRIC and is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a word for violent or intense, so more intense or ferocious.

clue.text: Viable plan to trap pub rodent

indicators.note: to trap means to enclose, so the pub letters sit inside the plan

parts.note: a goer is an idea or plan likely to succeed
PH, short for public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: A workable scheme for catching a pest in the local bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'goer' is British for a plan that works; PH is public house.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing North American animal with cheek pouches is one kind of rodent.

clue.text: People making peanuts heading for insolvency in opening story

indicators.note: in places the brand and the letter inside the opening

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in skin
KP is a British snack brand known for its salted peanuts

indicators.note: heading for points to the first letter of insolvency

explanation.surface: A tale of poorly paid workers going bust right at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making peanuts' suggests low pay, but KP is the British nut brand. PORKPIE is rhyming slang for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a pork pie, or porky, means a lie, a made-up tale.

clue.text: See 16
Vegetable issue inspiring panic at first, beetle reportedly beginning to nibble on one

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the son takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of panic

parts.note: beetle sounds like Beatle, and Ringo Starr was a Beatle

indicators.note: in an across clue, the nibble letter set on the one means it comes just before it
beginning to points to the first letter of nibble

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A vegetable crop panics as a beetle starts to chew it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' makes beetle sound like Beatle, and the Beatle is Ringo Starr. 'inspiring' (breathing in) puts all the inner pieces inside the son.
explanation.definitionFit: This young onion with a long green stalk, eaten raw in salads, is an example of a vegetable.

clue.text: Ship — that which you can bet on having capsized

indicators.note: capsized means turned upside down, so the betting word is read upwards

parts.words: that which you can bet on
parts.note: the football pools are a British betting game on match results

explanation.surface: A boat that gamblers wager on has overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: The pools are a British weekly bet on football scores.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-masted sailing vessel is a kind of ship.

clue.text: Squares introduced to fashion, in essence

indicators.note: introduced to means placed within, so the letters are found inside the words

explanation.surface: Conservative types are brought into fashion, essentially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squares' looks like fogeys, but nine is three squared.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is three times three, so the numbers are square numbers.

clue.text: Rotten muck in gesture

indicators.note: in places the muck inside the gesture

parts.note: a nod is a gesture of the head
goo is sticky muck

explanation.surface: Muck appears in a gesture, which is rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthless or bad is called useless or rotten.

clue.text: Something found in kitchen, one-legged pig hiding in empty cupboard

indicators.note: hiding in means concealed inside the emptied cupboard
empty means with the inside removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: moving on one leg is hopping
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A lame pig is hiding in a bare cupboard in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves only the outer letters of 'cupboard'; the hopping boar is a one-legged pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden or plastic slab for slicing food is a typical kitchen item.

clue.text: Turn back on man while sleeping?

indicators.note: while sleeping means in bed, so the letter goes inside the sleeping place

parts.note: where one is while sleeping is bed

indicators.note: back on points to the final letter of man

explanation.surface: A sleeper rolls over, turning away from a man in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The back of 'man' is N; a man 'while sleeping' is in bed, so N goes into BED.
explanation.definitionFit: A bend in a road is a turn or curve.

clue.text: Worry about itinerant pal lacking support

indicators.note: about means round, so the worry goes round the rearranged pal

parts.note: stress is worry

indicators.note: itinerant means wandering, so the letters of pal move around

explanation.surface: Fretting over a drifting friend who has nobody to back them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'itinerant' rearranges the letters of 'pal' into APL, which the worry goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress or bra with no shoulder straps has nothing holding it up.
